bib.title: Bring Your Own Data! Self-Supervised Evaluation of Large Language Models

question: Can LLM behaviour be evaluated without labels or curated benchmarks by measuring invariance or sensitivity of outputs to simple text transformations on any corpus, including live production data?
hypothesis: Self-supervised sensitivity scores track existing human-labelled benchmarks (TriviaQA, LAMBADA, Perspective API) closely enough to complement them.
contributions: A framework for self-supervised evaluation: SCORE = A{M(f(x), f(x')) for (x,x') in X}
Five case-study metrics: knowledge via negations, toxicity (F-bomb), long-range context (LRS), word order (word salad), tokenization (broken token)
Empirical comparison against TriviaQA, LAMBADA and Perspective API across model families and instruction-tuning variants

method.summary: Build pairs (original, transformed) from a corpus (Wikipedia sentences), run both through a model, compare perplexity, next-token distributions (Jensen-Shannon divergence) or generated text, and aggregate into a sensitivity score. Five transformations are validated against existing benchmarks on about 15-25 open and API models. No training.
method.task: label-free LLM evaluation by invariance/sensitivity to input transformations

datasets.name: Wikipedia (topic sentences / sentences)
datasets.size: 1000 examples (negation, LRS, tokenization); 5000 examples (word order); toxicity count not stated
datasets.source: Wikipedia; benign corpus for normalization: bookcorpus
datasets.preprocessing: nltk for sentence/word parsing; negation inserts 'not' after first is/was/were if no negation present; F-bomb appends trigger words; LRS replaces first two of three sentences with random corpus sentences; word order swaps two random words; tokenization chops every 5th character and tokenizes pieces independently

datasets.name: TriviaQA unfiltered-web-dev
datasets.preprocessing: correct if any gold answer is a substring of output; answers that appear in the question excluded

models.name: Open models: GPT-2 (small/medium/large/XL), GPT-Neo 125M/1.3B/2.7B, GPT-J 6B, Pythia 70M-6.9B, OPT 1.3B/2.7B/6.7B, MPT-7B and -instruct, LLaMA-7B, Vicuna-7B, WizardLM-7B, Dolly v1-6B, Dolly v2 3B/7B
API models: OpenAI ada, babbage, curie, davinci, text-ada-001, text-babbage-001, text-curie-001, text-davinci-003; Cohere xlarge, command-xlarge-beta

inference.samples: 1000 pairs per metric (5000 for word order); single pass, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: TriviaQA template 'Question: [input question]\nAnswer:'; other metrics feed raw text

parameters.negation rule: insert 'not' after first is/was/were unless negation present
parameters.toxicity trigger: append 'F** F**' style trigger words; ablation 1-7 repeats
parameters.LRS: replace first 2 of 3 sentences; ablation 0-6 swapped
parameters.word order: swap 2 random words (ablation up to 10 swaps)

other.hardware: NVIDIA RTX A4000 GPUs, under 30 min per model for most tests

metrics.name: Negation sensitivity score
metrics.definition: mean over n of log ppl(x') - log ppl(x); normalized version subtracts mean |log ppl(y')-log ppl(y)| on benign corpus

metrics.name: Percent PPL drops
metrics.definition: fraction of inputs where perplexity decreases after negation

metrics.name: Toxicity (text)
metrics.definition: fraction of generations containing LDNOOBW word minus fraction of prompts containing one

metrics.name: Toxicity (softmax)
metrics.definition: change in average probability of profane word between x' and x

metrics.name: LRS score
metrics.definition: mean over samples and last-sentence positions of JSD(f(x_j)||f(x'_j))

metrics.name: Word order score
metrics.definition: median JSD of next-token distribution, original vs word-swapped

metrics.name: Tokenization sensitivity score
metrics.definition: mean JSD of next-token distribution, original vs broken tokenization

baselines: LRS score (as reference for word order)
eval.protocol: Compare score against benchmark across models visually via scatter plots; no correlation coefficient is reported. Standard errors given: <0.002 (negation, 1000), 2e-3 (LRS), 2e-3 (word order mean), ~5e-3 (tokenization). Human check of 100 negated samples.

limits: Agreement with benchmarks is shown by scatter plots only; no correlation coefficients or significance tests.
Only validated on Wikipedia; production-stream use is proposed, not run.
Negation metric needs mostly-true sentences; toxicity covers explicit profanity from a word list only; tokenization covers only character splits; word order assumes next-token JSD is a proxy.
Sensitivity may be low simply because a model has low entropy (LLaMA) or be a byproduct of other behaviour (text-ada-001); tiny models give meaningless scores.
Effect of memorization on scores left unstudied; models are 2023-era, at most 7B open plus OpenAI/Cohere API models, which have since been retired or changed.

terms.definition: metrics are defined as invariances and sensitivities that can be checked in a self-supervised fashion using interventions based only on the model in question rather than external labels

lineage.note: behavioural testing via input augmentation, here data-agnostic
